study.title: Daniel 10 - the vision, spiritual warfare, and the word of truth
study.overview: Daniel 10 opens the last great vision of the book and prepares the detailed content that will be presented later. The chapter shows Daniel in grief and fasting, receiving a revelation that physically slaughters him, but also comforts him and re-ergued him. The focus is not only on the heavenly messenger, but on the fact that God's response had already been given from the first day, even if there was spiritual opposition attached to the human realms. The chapter ends with the promise that the message proceeds from what is written in the truth of God, with Michael acting in favor of the people of Daniel.

outline.title: Preparation for humiliation and fasting
outline.explanation: Daniel receives a true word about a great war and therefore goes into mourning for three weeks. His abstinence from pleasant food, flesh, wine and ointment shows an attitude of sobriety and distress before revelation. At the end of this period, he is by the Tigris River, ready to receive the vision.

outline.title: The glorious manifestation and the first word of encouragement
outline.explanation: Daniel sees a man dressed in linen with overwhelming appearance, and those accompanying him fleeing taken from dread. The vision takes away all the strength of Daniel, who falls into deep sleep. The messenger touches him, the flame of much dear and states that his words were heard from the first day, although there were spiritual resistance attached to the prince of Persia for twenty-one days.

outline.title: The Explanated Mission and the Invisible Conflict
outline.explanation: The messenger says that he came to make Daniel understood about what would happen to his people in the last days. Daniel runs out of voice, gets new touch and encouragement to stay firm. Finally, the messenger reveals that he will return to face the prince of Persia and that the prince of Greece will also come, but everything is being communicated from what is written in the scripture of the truth, with Michael as the only additional ally in that struggle.

study.context: The chapter is in the third year of Cyrus, king of Persia. Tyndale's note informs that this corresponds to a period shortly after the decree of return from exile, so that Daniel's distress is not for lack of God's response, but probably because of other visions and the weight of the future. The notes also indicate that Daniel is receiving the opening for the rest of the revelation that will be detailed in the next chapter.
study.theology: Daniel 10 teaches that divine revelation is true and sovereign, even when its fulfillment seems lengthy. The text also clearly affirms the reality of spiritual conflict behind human history: there is opposition linked to the kingdoms of the earth, but God rules over everything. God's response is not annulled by resistance, only delayed in the historical unfolding. The chapter also shows that the servant of God can be deeply shaken by holiness and heavenly glory, but is sustained by touch, word and peace. For a Protestant evangelical reading, this points to the dependence on God's grace, to the seriousness of prayer and to the confidence that the Lord knows and directs the course of history and his people.

scholarViews.insight: The "write of truth" indicates that the message proceeds from the record of God's will, and Michael appears as the spiritual prince of Israel, in contrast to the spiritual princes of the nations.
Daniel is sure that his words were heard from the first day, although the answer had been delayed, which shows that the delay does not mean divine rejection.
The expression concerning the "write of truth" can allude to what had already been written, and Michael is seen as the angel appointed by God in favor of the Jewish nation.

questions: How does the reality of an answer already heard by God help to endure when the visible response takes time?
What does this chapter teach about the relationship between human decisions and invisible spiritual conflicts?
How does Daniel's reverence before the vision correct our tendency to treat God's things superficially?
study.practice: Separate an intentional time of prayer with fasting or sobriety, if this is possible and prudent for you, to seek discernment in the face of a difficult situation. In doing so, remember that the apparent silence of God does not mean absence of him. Read Scripture with humility, ask for understanding and persevere, trusting that the Lord already knows the truth of his future. Also practice reverence: reduce distractions, pray with sincerity, and accept that the glory of God strengthens us before we fully comfort us.
study.uncertainty: The biblical text and notes do not safely identify the exact identity of the man dressed in linen; the notes interpret the figure in a heavenly way and, in Matthew Henry, as an apparition of the Son of God, but this should be treated as interpretation. There are also not enough details in the given notes to accurately define all aspects of the spiritual warfare mentioned beyond what the chapter itself states. The phrase "last days" is maintained according to the text, with no additional chronological specification in the notes.
